title: Measurement and Verification — Baseline Methods of the Demand Response Programs
content:
## Baseline methods

The baseline is the estimate of the load a customer would have used during an event had no event been called. Each of the Demand Response Programs estimates it, or measures performance without it, as follows; the pool size is the number of similar non-event days the method draws on, and 0 means that no baseline is computed.

| Program | How the load the customer would have used is estimated | Similar non-event days in the baseline pool |
|---|---|---|
| Peak Time Rebate | Average usage in the event hours on the 3 highest of the 10 most recent similar non-event weekdays | 10 |
| Smart Thermostat Rewards | Device telemetry; no baseline computed | 0 |
| AC Cycling Program | Device telemetry; no baseline computed | 0 |
| Home Battery Dispatch | Device telemetry; delivered kW is average battery discharge over the event hours | 0 |
| Commercial Capacity Bidding Program | Average of the 10 most recent similar non-event weekdays in the event hours, adjusted by the morning ratio capped at 20 percent | 10 |
| Base Interruptible Program | Firm service level committed by the customer | 0 |

## Method notes

- **Peak Time Rebate** draws on the 10 most recent similar non-event weekdays, keeps the 3 with the highest usage in the event hours, and takes the average of those 3.
- **Commercial Capacity Bidding Program** takes the average of all 10 of the most recent similar non-event weekdays in the event hours, adjusted by the morning ratio, the adjustment being capped at 20 percent.
- **Smart Thermostat Rewards and the AC Cycling Program** compute no baseline; performance is read from device telemetry.
- **Home Battery Dispatch** computes no baseline; the delivered kW is the average battery discharge over the event hours, read from device telemetry.
- **Base Interruptible Program** uses the firm service level the customer has committed to in place of an estimated baseline.

## Worked illustration — Peak Time Rebate (hypothetical figures)

A residential customer's usage in the event hours on the 10 most recent similar non-event weekdays is, in kWh: 6.2, 5.8, 7.2, 6.4, 5.5, 6.0, 7.5, 6.6, 5.9 and 6.9.

- The 3 highest days are 7.5, 7.2 and 6.9 kWh.
- Their total is 21.6 kWh; divided by 3, the baseline is 7.2 kWh for the event hours.
- The other 7 days do not enter the average.
